name: Mat-Su Salmon Partnership NFHP Funding Call
summary: Annual call for salmon habitat projects in Alaska's Mat-Su Basin, passing proposals to the National Fish Habitat Partnership for funding: riparian and instream restoration, barrier removal, habitat assessment and monitoring.

amount.note: Regional projects; larger projects will be considered

steps: NFHP Board review and potential selection

eligibility.rule: Has capacity to receive federal funds and satisfy funding reporting requirements
Has the capabilities and experience to implement the proposed project
Provides measurable goals and objectives for maintaining or restoring fish habitat
Identifies appropriate monitoring and evaluation measures and criteria
Addresses one or more goals and objectives from the MSSHP Conservation Action Plan
Does not fall under permit compliance, mitigation, or political advocacy
Meets at least six of the 13 ACE Act "soft" project criteria

documents: Landowner support letter, for easement or restoration activity
Landowner approval letters, including State of Alaska approval, for land acquisition

status.quote: Project proposals are due via email by 11:59pm (AKST) on Monday, September 14, 2026.

deadline.quote: Project proposals are due via email by 11:59pm (AKST) on Monday, September 14, 2026.

geography.quote: It was formed to provide a broad-based coordinated response to increasing impacts on salmon habitat from human use and development in the Mat-Su Basin.

access.quote: Applicants need to prepare and submit a project proposal that describes their project and its benefits for fish habitat.

window.quote: is announcing its annual invitation for fish habitat conservation project proposals for Federal Fiscal Year 2027 (FY27)

amount.quote: be available to cover 3-6 regional projects ranging from $10,000 to $75,000, but larger projects will be considered.

co_finance_required.quote: Although match at the individual project level is no longer required

applicant_types.quote: Any individual or organization can apply who has the capacity to receive federal funds and satisfy funding reporting requirements.

effort.quote: Project proposals are due via email by 11:59pm (AKST) on Monday, September 14, 2026.

The MSBSHP Steering Committee will use the scoring criteria listed in Attachment 2 to evaluate proposals which fall under four main categories: Resource Benefits, Technical Merit, Budget, and Timeline for Completion.
routed to the NFHP Board for their review and potential selection based upon available FY27 funding opportunities.

Once selected projects are approved by the NFHP Board and Secretary of the Interior, applicants selected for funding will be sent additional instructions, a GrantSolutions Directed Announcement identification number where all application documentation must be submitted, and a submission deadline.

eligibility.quote: Any individual or organization can apply who has the capacity to receive federal funds and satisfy funding reporting requirements.
Does the project sponsor have capabilities and experience to successfully implement the proposed project?
Does project provide measurable goals and objectives towards maintaining or restoring fish habitat?
Does proposal identify appropriate monitoring and evaluation measures and criteria?
Does proposal address one or more goals and objectives from the MSSHP Conservation Action Plan?
Projects that fall under permit compliance, mitigation, and political advocacy are not eligible.
All projects require an outreach component, whether it is informing the public at a community meeting or creating a small article or news release in the local paper.
In addition, projects are required to meet at least six of the 13 "soft" project criteria identified in the ACE Act (see "soft" ACE ACT criteria below).

after_award.quote: Yes, there will be annual progress and financial status reports with each approved project.

documents.quote: A landowner support letter (or letters) is required for any easement or restoration activity proposed.
